title: SemVer-led lifecycle orchestration and cross-surface compatibility ledger
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We lack a single, machine-readable source of truth that ties semantic versioning, runtime ABI guarantees, API surface changes, SDK deprecation timelines, and Console UX migration windows together. This ambiguity causes last-minute coordination work across runtime, API, SDK, and Console teams during upgrades and leads to avoidable rollbacks and inconsistent customer messaging.

Goal: Create a canonical "compatibility ledger" and enforcement pipeline that: (1) defines semver-to-compatibility mappings for runtime, API, SDK, and Console; (2) provides rollout gate rules (preflight checks, canary cohorts, automated rollback heuristics); (3) integrates with CI/CD to surface breaking-change flags and release notes; and (4) powers Console upgrade UI + SDK warnings.

Out-of-scope: Full automation of cluster-level upgrades for Dedicated; that will be handled in a follow-on epic. This ticket focuses on policy, metadata, gating checks, and the integration points for runtime, API, SDKs, and Console.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable compatibility ledger schema (YAML/JSON) exists and lives in the repo: spec/compatibility-ledger/v1.yaml
SemVer mapping rules documented: major -> potential breaking change, minor -> additive but may change behavior, patch -> bugfix only
Runtime ABI matrix published that maps runtime-2.x kernels and quantization profiles to supported model formats
API compatibility rules and SDK pinning recommendations surfaced in SDK release pipeline (automated CI warnings for pinned-major mismatches)
Console shows per-customer recommended upgrade window and will block forced upgrades if preflight checks fail
Rollout gate prototypes implemented: preflight (canary traffic test), metrics-based gate (latency/error SLO thresholds), and automated rollback trigger (error delta + increase in 5xx rate)
Integration tests that fail when a proposed release violates ledger constraints are added to release CI
Confluence spec and an initial migration playbook (runbook) shared with Eng/PM/Design and approved by the Release Council
implementation_plan: Draft ledger schema and mapping rules (semver -> surface guarantees) and PR to infra/specs repository
Add ledger validator to release CI that checks proposed release metadata against ledger rules
Define and implement three standard rollout gate templates in the rollout service: preflight, metrics-gate, and canary cohorts
Instrument SDK release pipeline to emit compatibility warnings and to auto-create follow-ups for major bumps
Add Console UI components to fetch ledger entries and render per-release guidance + block button for forced upgrades
Coordinate with runtime team to produce an ABI support table and attach model/quantization caveats
Run internal dogfooding: upgrade a non-critical staging tenant using the new ledger and gates and capture lessons
Publish runbook and onboard Release Ops with a 1-hour smoke checklist
design_decisions: Ledger format: YAML primary with JSON-LD view for programmatic consumers to ease integration with Console and CI
SemVer policy: strict semantic versioning with explicitly declared exceptions (opt-outs) for runtime kernel tweaks that do not change public API
Gate thresholds: use relative delta heuristics for SLOs (e.g., 20% degradation over baseline OR absolute increase >0.5% error rate) to reduce brittle thresholds
Rollback strategy: automated rollback only when both error delta and latency delta exceed thresholds AND customer-impact flag is low/medium; high-impact releases require manual confirmation
Console integration approach: read-only ledger consumer in Console with guidance and soft blocks; critical blocks require Release Ops override
risks: Maintaining the ledger will add ongoing operational overhead and requires clear ownership (risk: drift between ledger and actual runtime guarantees)
Overly conservative gates may slow releases and frustrate product teams; overly permissive gates reduce value
Edge cases where runtime kernel changes affect outputs subtly (quality regressions) may not be caught by metrics-based gates
SDK pinning enforcement could break downstream customer CI if we force-bump major versions without migration helpers
notes: We should align ledger entries with model compatibility artifacts produced by the model-onboarding team (pointer in ledger entry)
Consider adding an audit webhook so customers with Private deployments can subscribe to ledger changes
Plan to expose a /compatibility endpoint on the API for programmatic queries by SDKs and Console
Discussed using feature flags for migrations where behavior changes are non-trivial; flagged for follow-up
